```{r}
#pivoting data, reshaping a dataset
install.packages("tidyr")
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

# wide fomart - each variable gets its own column, easy for humans to read 
# long formart - one row per measurment with a column naming which variabe it is.- easy for R to group filter and plot

wide_data <- data.frame(
  patient = c(1, 2),
  day1_temp = c(37.2, 36.9),
  day2_temp = c(38.1, 37.0),
  day3_temp = c(37.5, 36.8)
)
wide_data
View(wide_data)
long_data <- wide_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(day1_temp, day2_temp, day3_temp),  # which columns to stack
    names_to = "day",                            # new column holding the old column names
    values_to = "temp"                            # new column holding the actual values
  )
long_data
View(long_data)

symptoms_long <- linelist %>%
  select(case_id, fever, chills, cough, aches, vomit) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(fever, chills, cough, aches, vomit),
    names_to = "symptom",
    values_to = "status"
  )
symptoms_long %>%
  filter(status == "yes") %>%
  count(symptom) %>%
  arrange(desc(n))
```
```{r}
#merging datasets 
patients <- data.frame(
  case_id = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  age = c(34, 51, 22, 45)
)

hospitals <- data.frame(
  case_id = c(1, 2, 3),
  hospital_name = c("St. Mary's", "General", "St. Mary's")
)
#left_join() keeps every row from thr first table and pulls in info from the second.

combined <- patients %>%
  left_join(hospitals, by = "case_id")

inner_join()
combined_inner <- patients %>%
  inner_join(hospitals, by = "case_id")
combined_inner
```

```{r}
combined_full <- patients %>%
  full_join(hospitals, by = "case_id")
```
